key_insight: A Quantum Circuit Born Machine can generate high-fidelity synthetic tabular samples that help correct class imbalance and improve minority-class prediction.
engineering_relevance: The work suggests a practical quantum-classical augmentation pipeline for structured data settings where traditional oversampling may miss complex data distributions.
method: Normalize data and reduce dimensions with PCA for efficient quantum basis encoding.
Train a parameterized QCBM to match the real data distribution by minimizing KL divergence with parameter-shift gradients.
Augment minority-class training data with QCBM-generated samples and compare against SMOTE variants.
evidence_signal: On Iris and Telco churn, adding 40-50% QCBM synthetic minority samples improved F1 by about 5-15% and minority recall by 10-25%, with only a 3-10% gap in cross-domain train/test evaluations.
watch_item: The approach depends on careful preprocessing and low-dimensional tabular structure, so scaling to higher-dimensional or noisy real-world data may be challenging.
paper_title: Quantum-Enhanced Synthetic Data Generation Using Quantum Circuit Born Machines for Imbalanced Tabular Learning
